questions.question: _________ is an asset that the borrower owns (such as land, building, vehicle, livestock, deposits with banks) and uses this as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Collateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An asset that the borrower owns and uses this as a guarantee to the lender until the loan is repaid is called collateral.
 
• Credit in economics is a contractual agreement, in which a borrower agrees to repay the lender at a later date for some value received now, generally with some interest.
 
• A loan is anything such as goods, money, or property which are lent by an individual in exchange for future repayment.
 
• A bond, in simpler terms, is a debt security, from the bond issuer to the holders.

questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was devised by Governor General _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Dalhousie served as Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.

 
 
• Governor-General known as the 'maker of modern India'.
 
• The widow remarriage act was introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1855.
 
• He abolished the titles and pensions in British India.
 
• He introduced the doctrine of lapse.
 
• Public Works Department in India was founded by Dalhousie.
 
• Passenger trains in railways, electric telegraph, and uniform postage in India were introduced during his tenure.
 
• Lord Dalhousie was the viceroy who started the first railway line in India in 1853(connecting Bombay to Thane).
 
• He is the Governor-General who appointed 'Wood's education commission'.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The principle of lapsed

 
 
• The doctrine was introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1848.
 
• The doctrine stated that any Indian princely state under the suzerainty of the East India Company would have its princely status abolished and be annexed into directly ruled British India if the ruler was either "manifestly incompetent or died without a male heir".
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was used by Lord Dalhousie to annex several princely states, including **Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Jhansi, and Nagpur**.
 
• The doctrine was a controversial policy, and it was one of the factors that contributed to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• The doctrine was repealed by Lord Ripon in 1884.

questions.question: _________, the constitutional head of India, has a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to advise him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President of India is the constitutional head of the Executive of the Union.
 
• As per the Constitution, the President is the supreme commander of the defense forces of India.
 
• The President of India exercises executive powers on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President represents the unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament, as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President holds office for a term of five years and is eligible for re-election.
 
• In the event of a vacancy due to death, resignation, or removal, the Vice President serves as the acting President until a new President is elected.
 
• The President has the power to appoint the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice and other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and various other constitutional positions.
 
• The President also has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense.

questions.question: In India, the dependency ratio of children is a measure of the number of dependents aged
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 to 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Index of Ageing (Ageing Index) is a demographic indicator that provides insights into the age structure of a population. It measures the relative size of the elderly population (aged 60 years and above) in comparison to the young population (aged 0-14 years) within a given population or geographic area.
 
• The index is calculated by dividing the population aged 60 years and above by the population aged 0-14 years and then multiplying the result by 100 to express it as a percentage.

 An Ageing Index of 100 or greater indicates that the elderly population (60 years and above) is equal to or larger than the population of children (0-14 years). This suggests an aging population and is a key demographic feature of many developed and developing countries.
 
• The Ageing Index serves as a valuable tool for understanding the age distribution within a population.
 
• A higher Ageing Index suggests that a larger proportion of the population is in the elderly age group relative to children.
 
• Demographers and policymakers use this index to assess the potential implications of an aging population. It can inform planning and policy decisions in various areas, including healthcare, social services, and labor markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Youth Dependency Ratio: This ratio is calculated by dividing the population aged 0-14 years by the population aged 15-64 years. It reflects the proportion of the population that is considered economically dependent, primarily children who are not in the workforce.
 
• Elderly Dependency Ratio: This ratio is calculated by dividing the population aged 65 years and above by the population aged 15-64 years. It reflects the proportion of the population that is considered economically dependent, primarily older individuals who are retired and not in the workforce.
 
• The dependency ratio is a demographic indicator that provides insights into the age structure of a population and the potential economic and social burdens associated with different age groups. It measures the proportion of economically dependent individuals (those who are typically not in the workforce) relative to the working-age population. 

Thus, the Ratio of the population aged 60 (sixty) years and above per 100 of the population aged 0 - 14 years is called the Index of Ageing.

• The Indian Census 2011 can be referred to as the seventh census operation after Indian independence.
 
• According to the State Census 2011,
 
 
• The most populated state in India is Uttar Pradesh with a population of 19.96 crores.

questions.question: Which dance style is incorporated with both the Tandava and Lasya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Manipuri:**

__
 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• This dance form originates from the** northeastern state of Manipur** in India.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• It includes both **Tandava and Lasya**, blending vigorous movements (representing Tandava) and soft, graceful movements (representing Lasya).
 
• Known for its devotional themes, Manipuri dances are often performed as an offering to gods, particularly** Lord Krishna and Radha**.
 
• The **male performers usually depict Tandava** through martial and vigorous expressions, while** female performers emphasize Lasya** with soft and elegant movements.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Odissi:**

 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from **Odisha**.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• It is characterized by fluid, graceful movements, including **Tribhangi posture **(three bends of the body).
 
• Primarily focuses on **Lasya (feminine, graceful)** and **devotional expression to Lord Jagannath**.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect:** Odissi does not have significant elements of Tandava; it leans more towards Lasya.

**Kathak:**

 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• This dance form is rooted in **North India** and is linked to storytelling traditions.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• Kathak emphasizes **intricate footwork, fast spins, and expressive gestures**.
 
• It includes energetic movements but is primarily focused on the **rhythmic **aspect rather than a balance of Tandava and Lasya.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect: **While Kathak has moments of vigor (which may seem like Tandava), it lacks a deliberate and distinct representation of both Tandava and Lasya.

**Bharatanatyam:**

 
• **Origin: **

 
 
• **​**Bharatanatyam hails from **Tamil Nadu **in South India.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a **highly expressive dance** form with distinct **Nritta **(pure dance) and **Abhinaya **(expression).
 
• It primarily showcases Lasya but has elements of Tandava in certain vigorous performances like depicting Lord Shiva's cosmic dance.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect: **Though Bharatanatyam includes Tandava elements, it is not as balanced as Manipuri in integrating both Tandava and Lasya equally
